title: RowBrief · CSV handoff checker
shortDescription: Inspect CSVs locally. Compare delimiters, locate issues and share a report without cell values. Free MIT source.

faq.question: What is RowBrief for?
faq.answer: Understanding a CSV structure before handing it to someone else, with explicit parsing choices and a report that omits cell values.

faq.question: Does my file leave the browser?
faq.answer: The app reads it locally and makes no upload or analytics request. It saves no file, report or preference to browser storage. Hosting still receives ordinary page requests.

faq.question: What does a report include?
faq.answer: Delimiter/header/blank-record choices, BOM and line-ending metadata, counts and generic findings with source locations. Cell values, header names, source excerpts and filename are omitted. Counts/locations remain; review before sharing.

faq.question: Can it fix or convert a file?
faq.answer: No. The on-disk original is never modified, and no cleaned CSV or encoding conversion is exported. Files must be valid UTF-8.

faq.question: What are the limits?
faq.answer: 2 MiB, 10,000 parsed records including blanks, 100 fields per record, first 200 findings, and 20 preview records per page. Cell display is clipped to 200 characters.

faq.question: What is not checked?
faq.answer: Business rules, data types, formula safety and universal spreadsheet compatibility. Values render as text. A structural pass does not certify data quality or safety.

faq.question: How do I run and license it?
faq.answer: Use the free hosted tool or Node.js 22+, npm ci and npm start. Original code, docs, examples and artwork use MIT. No paid service, account or key is required. Community support has no response-time promise.
